title: chore(lock): Move LockService into libs/unlock and add lock/unlock source tracking
body:
## 🎟️ Tracking
https://bitwarden.atlassian.net/browse/PM-41447

## 📔 Objective
We need unlock and lock source tracking to prevent an instant re-lock caused by shared unlock. To do so, the callers of lock / unlock need to provide a lock source. In the case of unlock, this is done in the unlock service. In the case of lock, this is provided by the callers (vault timeout, manual UI lock, shared unlock).

This also in the same step moves the lock service to KM ownership, because auth does not own lock / unlock, and it was only owned by auth for historical reasons.

Note that the move of the service, and the addition of the lock source are combined into one PR to have fewer review round-trips, since these often touch the same files.

## 📸 Screenshots

N/A — no UI changes.

reviews.body: Love the new lock source introduction + KM taking ownership of lock! Thank you! Just 1 question about another file move 👇

inline.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT**: `UnlockSource.SharedUnlock` is never emitted — shared-unlock unlocks are reported as `Manual`.

<details>
<summary>Details and fix</summary>

`JsSharedUnlockDriver.unlock_user` (`libs/common/src/key-management/shared-unlock/shared-unlock-driver.ts:52`) unlocks via `unlockService.unlockWithDecryptedUserKey(...)`, and `DefaultUnlockService.unlockWithDecryptedUserKey` hardcodes `UnlockSource.Manual` (`libs/unlock/src/default-unlock.service.ts:172`). So every `registerOnUnlockAction` listener sees `Manual`, including the follower/leader callbacks that re-broadcast `ManualUnlock` back to the SDK — the exact echo this source tracking is meant to let listeners filter out.

Two options:
- Let the shared-unlock driver pass its source (e.g. an extra param on `unlockWithDecryptedUserKey`, or a dedicated entry point) so the value is actually produced.
- If wiring is deliberately deferred, add the same "nothing reports this yet" note used for `Auto` so consumers don't branch on a value that can never arrive.

The lock direction is already handled correctly (`LockSource.SharedUnlock` at `shared-unlock-driver.ts:44`), which makes the unlock direction look like an oversight rather than a deliberate deferral.
</details>
inline.diffHunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+/**
+ * What caused an unlock. Handed to every callback registered through
+ * {@link UnlockService.registerOnUnlockAction} so a listener can tell the unlocks it caused itself
+ * apart from the ones it should react to.
+ */
+export const UnlockSource = Object.freeze({
+  /**
+   * The user unlocked this device themselves — master password, PIN, biometrics, key connector,
+   * PRF, or logging in with another device.
+   */
+  Manual: "manual",
+  /**
+   * The vault was restored from the never-lock key rather than unlocked by anyone.
+   *
+   * Nothing reports this yet: the never-lock restore in `UserAutoUnlockKeyService` sets the user key
+   * directly instead of going through `UnlockService`.
+   */
+  Auto: "auto",
+  /** Another device unlocked this one over the shared unlock protocol. */
+  SharedUnlock: "sharedUnlock",

inline.body:
♻️ **DEBT**: This introduces a package-level cycle between `@bitwarden/unlock` and `@bitwarden/auth`.

<details>
<summary>Details and fix</summary>

`@bitwarden/auth` already depends on `@bitwarden/unlock` (e.g. `libs/auth/src/common/login-strategies/password-login.strategy.ts:26`, `libs/auth/src/common/services/login-strategies/login-strategy.service.ts:40` import `UnlockService`). With this move, `@bitwarden/unlock` now imports back into `@bitwarden/auth/common` for `LogoutService`.

It compiles today because `LogoutService` is only used as a type here, so the import is elided — but nothing prevents the next value-level import from making it a real runtime cycle. `libs/unlock` has no entry in the "Bandaids for keeping existing circular dependencies from getting worse and new ones from being created" block in `eslint.config.mjs`, so the boundary check that would flag this for a KM-owned lib (`KEY_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN_PACKAGES` lists `@bitwarden/auth`) doesn't apply here.

Worth either relocating the `LogoutService` abstraction out of `@bitwarden/auth/common`, or adding an explicit `libs/unlock/src/**/*.ts` boundary entry documenting that this one import is the accepted exception.
</details>

⚠️ **IMPORTANT**: `UnlockSource.SharedUnlock` is never emitted — shared-unlock unlocks are reported as `Manual`.

<details>

So every `registerOnUnlockAction` listener sees `Manual`, including the follower/leader callbacks that re-broadcast `ManualUnlock` back to the SDK — the exact echo this source tracking is meant to let listeners filter out.

Two options:
- Let the shared-unlock driver pass its source (e.g. an overload/param on `unlockWithDecryptedUserKey`, or a dedicated entry point) so the value is actually produced.
- If wiring is deliberately deferred, add the same "nothing reports this yet" note used for `Auto` so consumers don't branch on a value that can never arrive.

The lock direction is already handled correctly (`LockSource.SharedUnlock` at `shared-unlock-driver.ts:44`), which makes the unlock direction look like an oversight rather than a deliberate deferral.
</details>

comments.body:
## 🤖 Bitwarden Claude Code Review

**Overall Assessment:** APPROVE

Reviewed the relocation of `LockService`/`DefaultLockService` from `@bitwarden/auth/common` into `@bitwarden/unlock` and the addition of `LockSource`/`UnlockSource` plumbing across browser, desktop, web, and CLI call sites. Call-site sources look correctly assigned (manual UI/commands → `Manual`, vault timeout and idle → `VaultTimeout`, shared-unlock driver → `SharedUnlock`), the browser foreground/background message contract carries `source` end-to-end, and the constructor-dependency removals (`SearchService`, `InternalMasterPasswordServiceAbstraction`) match every construction site and DI `deps` array. Both new source objects follow ADR-0025 (frozen const object plus derived type), and the moved spec was updated in step with the signature changes.

<details>
<summary>Code Review Details</summary>

- ⚠️ : `UnlockSource.SharedUnlock` is never emitted — the shared-unlock driver unlocks through `unlockWithDecryptedUserKey`, which hardcodes `Manual`
  - `libs/unlock/src/unlock-source.enum.ts:20`
- ♻️ : New package-level cycle between `@bitwarden/unlock` and `@bitwarden/auth`, with no boundary rule covering `libs/unlock`
  - `libs/unlock/src/lock.service.ts:3`

</details>
